limitations: Regional discovery is substantial but not exhaustive; source coverage is strongest in Charleston, Scottsdale, Jackson, and Ketchum.
Current association-directory membership and public operational details support some rows without a separately dated 2026 exhibition; those bases are explicitly recorded.
Rows sourced only to official operational pages may have undated hours or inventory. A live website is not a guarantee of uninterrupted physical opening; no telephone confirmations were performed.
Only U.S. cities supported by consulted sources are recorded. Additional undiscovered branches may exist.
Several weak-state candidate domains were inaccessible, parked, closed, or unrelated and were not converted to active-gallery assertions.

# BigTown Gallery is pleased to announce its 2026 season
BigTown Gallery is pleased to announce its 2026 season, opening with _Grand Finale_, an exhibition dedicated to the work of Hugh Townley (1923–2008), the acclaimed sculptor and printmaker whose more than five-decade career combined material rigor with inventive, deeply personal form. A frequent early presence at the gallery, Townley played a formative role in shaping its vision and community, bringing both his extensive experience—as a longtime educator at Brown University and an artist exhibited at institutions including the Museum of Modern Art—and his generous spirit of collaboration to its development. Known for his intricate wood constructions, dynamic reliefs, and later explorations in plywood and color, his work reflects a singular visual language informed by nature, Indigenous traditions, and global spiritual inquiry. The 2026 season will also feature the return of our FILM/TALK/FOOD series with the Wild and Scenic Film Festival’s _Best of the Fest_ selection, as well as the third year of _My Place Photography Workshop 3.0_, a professional development photography workshop led by Jim Dow and Cassandra Klos.
For more than two decades, BigTown Gallery has been rooted in a region shaped by independent artists working within a vital, alternative creative culture. Early on, we were drawn to a generation educated in the years following World War II—many supported by the GI Bill—whose influence helped establish the region’s respected MFA programs. Since then, the gallery has remained committed to presenting the depth and significance of their work, often through exhibitions that trace the arc of an artist’s career for a regional audience.
Now in its third decade, and in partnership with the nonprofit BigTown Projects, the gallery continues to expand its program with exhibitions by contemporary artists addressing the complexities of a changing world. At the same time, a core group of artists remains central to the gallery’s program and ongoing support.
Work is available through the BT—VT website, at exhibitions held in the gallery and at the Stable, and through select art fairs.

Sharon Brush and Marietta Patricia Leis are two artists whose quiet, powerful, and organic work complement each other perfectly. Sharon Brush approaches the construction of each of her vessels as a sculpture—working to create rhythm, flow, reverberation and quiet within each one. Intrigued by contrasts, she moves from slow, sweeping curves to staccato points and ridges; from enclosed space to open passage; from deeply textured surface to river-rock smoothness. Leis’ reductive, expressive visual practice is shaped out of experiments in material process and takes inspiration from the forms of nature, sense of place and the internal landscape. She uses minimal yet deep color palettes across a variety of mediums the viewer can lose themselves in.

This exhibition will feature the still life paintings of Jeanette Pasin Sloan, whose stunning realist paintings are featured in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Smithsonian Museum, National Gallery, and more. Jeanette Pasin Sloan taught herself to paint as a young mother, putting her children to bed early so she could paint at the kitchen table studio. She obsessively painted the reflective surfaces of her chrome toaster and silver teacups, these everyday objects which we all share and know intimately. Pasin Sloan later earned an MFA from the University of Chicago in art history, where she developed her passion for extending the techniques of old master painters. After mastering oil and watercolor, the artist created a series of fantastic lithographs with Landfall Press.

WILD by Nature Gallery celebrates its 29th
anniversary, along with more than 44 years of
photographing the Tetons by Henry H.

Holdsworth. Dedicated to capturing the natural
beauty of Jackson Hole and surrounding national
parks, the gallery features striking landscape and
wildlife photography by this renowned local artist.

Henry’s work has been featured in publications
such as National Geographic, National Wildlife,
and Nature’s Best. Visitors can explore and collect
his images as limited edition prints, notecards,
and locally inspired coffee table books that reflect
the spirit and scenery of the Greater Yellowstone
ecosystem.
